title: A teaching not for every ear
source_text: καὶ κατὰ τὸ περὶ τὴν Ἱερουσαλὴμ γίνεσθαι κολάσεις χωνευομένων, τῶν ἀναλαβόντων εἰς τὴν ἑαυτῶν τῆς ψυχῆς ὑπόστασιν τὰ ἀπὸ κακίας, τροπικῶς που ὀνομαζομένης μολίβδου· διὸ ἡ ἀνομία παρὰ τῷ Ζαχαρίᾳ ἐπὶ „τάλαντον μολίβδου“ ἐκαθέζετο. Ὅσα δ᾿ εἰς τὸν τόπον λεχθείη ἂν, οὔτε πᾶσιν οὔτε τοῦ παρόντος καιροῦ ἐστι διηγήσασθαι· ἀλλ᾿ οὐδ᾿ ἀκίνδυνον τὴν τῶν τοιούτων σαφήνειαν πιστεῦσαι γραφῇ. ἅτε τῶν πολῶν οὐ χρῃζόντων πλείονος διδασκαλίας παρὰ τὴν περὶ τῆς κατὰ τῶν ἁμαρτανόντων κολάσεως. εἰς γὰρ τὰ ὑπερέκεινα αὐτῆς οὐ χρήσιμον ἀναβαίνειν διὰ τοὺς μόγις φόβῳ τῆς αἰωνίου κολάσεως κἂν συστέλλοντας ἐπὶ ποσὸν τῆς κακίας καὶ τῶν ἀπ᾿ αὐτῆς ἁμαρτανομένων χύσιν. οὔτ᾿ οὖν τὸ διάγραμμα οὔτε Κέλσος οἶδε τὸν περὶ Γεέννης λόγον· ἐπεὶ οὔτ᾿ ἂν ἐκεῖνοι ζωγραφίας καὶ διαγράμματα ἐσεμνοποίουν ὡς δι᾿ αὐτῶν παριστάντες τὸ ἀληθὲς. οὔτ᾿ ἂν ὁ Κέλσος ἐν τῷ κατὰ Χριστιανῶν συγγράμματι τὰ μηδαμῶς ὑπὸ Χριστιανῶν λεγόμενα ἀλλά τινων, τάχα οὐδ᾿ ἔτι ὄντων ἀλλὰ πάντῃ ἐκλελοιπότων καὶ εἰς πάνυ ὀλίγους καὶ εὐαριθμήτους καταστάντων, ἐνετίθει ταῖς κατὰ Χριστιανῶν κατηγορίαις. καὶ ὥσπερ οὐ καθήκει τοῖς τὰ Πλάτωνος φιλοσοφοῦσιν ἀπολογεῖσθαι περὶ Ἐπικούρου καὶ τῶν ἀσεβῶν αὐτοῦ δογμάτων, οὕτως οὐδ᾿ ἡμῖν περὶ τῶν ἐν τῷ διαγράμματι καὶ τῶν κατ᾿ αὐτοῦ λεγομένων ὑπὸ Κέλσου. διόπερ ὡς περισσὰ καὶ μάτην ἐκκείμενα ἐῶμεν τὰ ὑπὸ Κέλσου εἰς ταῦτα λελεγμένα· μᾶλλον γὰρ Κέλσου ἡμεῖς αὐτῶν παρὰ τοῖς κεκρατημένοις ὑπὸ τοιούτων λόγων κατηγορήσομεν.
pass_a_gloss: And according to the (saying that) about Jerusalem punishments (κόλασις) happen of those being smelted (χωνεύω), of those who have taken up (ἀναλαμβάνω) into the substance (ὑπόστασις) of their own soul the things from vice (κακία), figuratively (τροπικῶς) somewhere named lead (μόλιβδος); wherefore lawlessness (ἀνομία) in Zechariah sat (καθέζομαι) upon 'a talent (τάλαντον) of lead'. Whatever might be said into (on) the topic (τόπος) is neither for all nor of the present occasion (καιρός) to narrate; but neither is it without danger (ἀκίνδυνος) to entrust (πιστεύω) the clarity (σαφήνεια) of such things to writing (γραφή), since the many do not need more teaching (διδασκαλία) beyond that about the punishment against those who sin. For into the things beyond (ὑπερέκεινα) it, it is not useful (χρήσιμος) to go up, because of those who barely (μόγις) by fear (φόβος) of the eternal (αἰώνιος) punishment check (συστέλλω) even to some extent the outpouring (χύσις) of vice and of the sins from it. So neither the diagram nor Celsus knows the account (λόγος) about Gehenna; since neither would those have made solemn (σεμνοποιέω) paintings (ζωγραφία) and diagrams as presenting (παρίστημι) the truth through them, nor would Celsus in the treatise (σύγγραμμα) against Christians have put into the accusations (κατηγορία) against Christians the things in no way said by Christians but by some, perhaps not even still existing but wholly having failed (ἐκλείπω) and come down to very few and easily counted (εὐαρίθμητος). And as it is not fitting (καθήκει) for those philosophizing the things of Plato to make defence (ἀπολογέομαι) about Epicurus and his impious (ἀσεβής) doctrines (δόγμα), so neither for us about the things in the diagram and those said against it by Celsus. Wherefore as superfluous (περισσός) and set out in vain (μάτην) we let be (ἐάω) the things said by Celsus on these; for we more than Celsus will accuse (κατηγορέω) them before those held fast (κρατέω) by such teachings (λόγοι).
pass_b_english: …and in keeping with the saying that around Jerusalem punishments come upon those who are being smelted (Ezekiel 22:18–22), those who have taken into the very substance of their own soul what comes from vice; and vice is somewhere called lead, in a figure. That is why, in Zechariah, lawlessness was sitting upon “a talent of lead” (Zechariah 5:7–8).

Whatever might be said on this subject is not for everyone, nor is this the time to set it out. Nor is it without danger to entrust a plain account of such things to writing, since the many need no further teaching than that about the punishment of sinners. For it is not useful to go up to what lies beyond it, because of those who, through fear of eternal punishment, barely check, even in some measure, the flood of vice and of the sins that come from it.

So neither the diagram nor Celsus knows the teaching about Gehenna. Otherwise those people would not have made so solemn a show of pictures and diagrams, as though they were presenting the truth through them; nor would Celsus, in his treatise against Christians, have inserted into his charges against Christians things in no way said by Christians, but by certain people who perhaps no longer even exist, but have wholly died out and dwindled to a very few, easily counted.

And just as it is not fitting for those who follow the philosophy of Plato to answer for Epicurus and his impious doctrines, so neither is it fitting for us to answer for what is in the diagram and for what Celsus says against it. Therefore we leave aside, as superfluous and set out to no purpose, what Celsus has said on these matters; for we ourselves will accuse those people more than Celsus does, before any who are held fast by such teachings.

choices.choice: Continues the sentence begun at the end of 6.25. ‘Punishments around Jerusalem of those being smelted’ is a clear allusion to Ezekiel 22:18–22, where Israel is bronze, tin, iron and lead gathered into the midst of Jerusalem and melted; this also explains why vice is ‘called lead’. Zechariah 5:7–8 LXX: a talent of lead, a woman sitting in the measure, ‘this is lawlessness’ (ἀνομία). ἅτε τῶν πολῶν is a misprint in the staged text for πολλῶν (‘the many’). ‘Flood of vice’ renders χύσιν (‘outpouring’). ‘Eternal punishment’ (αἰωνίου κολάσεως) recalls Matthew 25:46 in wording, but Origen is not quoting; left uncited. Origen’s reserve here about the further teaching on punishment is his own; nothing is added to explain it. Last sentence: παρὰ τοῖς κεκρατημένοις read as ‘before (in the presence of) those held fast’.
agency fixed: the fearful are the ones who check (συστέλλοντας, active) the flood of vice, not 'are held back' from it
ἀπολογεῖσθαι περί rendered 'answer for' (not 'make a defence for', which implied defending Epicurus)
κατηγορήσομεν is future indicative: 'would accuse' corrected to 'will accuse'
opening '…' marks that the sentence begins in 6.25 (καὶ κατὰ ...); not split

anf_compare.notes: Crombie (ANF 1872) and Chadwick (1953) were not used or consulted; the English is from the Greek.
